name: Calendar, write only
plain: Adds events to the calendar without reading anything already there.
meaning: Lets a ticketing or booking app add an event with no view of the person's schedule.

android.permission: None for ACTION_INSERT intent; WRITE_CALENDAR for direct writes
android.prompt_ui: ACTION_INSERT opens the system calendar editor, no permission
android.note: The intent path is the privacy first route

ios.note: EKEventEditViewController needs no permission on iOS 17 (out of process)

limits.headline: Can add events to your calendar without seeing anything already in it
limits.user_action: You tap Add to calendar on a ticket or booking
can: Open the system calendar editor with the event filled in, no permission needed
Add events directly once you allow it (Android) or choose add only access (iPhone)
Show you the editor so you save the event yourself
cannot: Change or delete events already there
Save the event without your tap when it uses the system editor
limits.differs: iPhone with iOS 17 and later offers a true add only choice; on Android the system editor is the privacy first route.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app add events to your calendar without being able to read what is already there.

marketing.name: EventKit write only access
marketing.pitch: Apps can add events to a calendar without seeing any of your existing events.

story.for_you: A prompt says the app wants to add events only. You tap Allow and the ticket lands in your calendar. The app never sees your meetings or your doctor visits.
story.for_makers: A ticket or booking app only needs to drop an event on the calendar. This option gets approval from careful users and avoids a scary full access prompt. It is a smart default for most apps.

use_cases.example: A ticket app puts a concert and the doors time on your calendar.
A flight app saves your outbound and return flights as events.
A booking app adds your gym class and updates it if the time changes.
A grocery app adds a delivery window so you remember to be home.
A clinic app adds the visit with no view of your other plans.
A course app adds each lecture and deadline.
A game adds a live event or tournament start time as a reminder.

story.android_note: Android has the same route through an intent that opens the calendar event screen with no permission.
story.ios_note: iOS 17 added write only access. The event edit screen runs outside the app and needs no permission.

technical_bounds: Cannot read back events on iOS write-only grant

history.change: Write-only access added; EKEventEditViewController runs without permission
